I'm currently working on a group project and am having problems with my LEDs. I'm hoping to use the concept of multiplexing to allow me to have a lot of LEDs connected to my Arduino Uno but am very very new to anything electronics. I'm not sure if I'm understanding multiplexing completely, but it seems that I wouldn't need to use this if I'm using an addressable LED strip, which is what I'm using (ws2812b).

Would I be able to use one continuous strip and have it turn different lights on and off quickly so that it looks like every light is lit at the same time? Is there a way I can calculate how fast I'd need to switch the lights on and off or is there a minimum number of lights I'd have to have on at any given time in order to have this effect? I apologize in advance for my lack of knowledge in the subject and if I've said anything completely stupid. Forgive me!

Multiplexing takes advantage that if you have a column that has is currently HIGH connecting to a row that is also HIGH the LED does not turn on allowing you to control more than 1 led per pin. but the down side is you cant have each row of leds on at the same time, by quickly turning a led on and off then moving to the next row and looping the display you can trick your eyes into thinking the lights do not turn off.

this effect is called Flicker fusion threshold see also Persistence of vision

you can also do things like use 4 pins to drive a shift register to allow you to control a large number of leds

X2 (5 by 7) led matrix

this uses 4 shift registers that have been daisy chained to each other

work in progress code (its a mess :P)

hope this helps
